articles.title: Tiny beetle trapped in 53-million-year-old amber is named after Twenty One Pilots
articles.source: Phys.org - latest science and technology news stories
articles.summary: Preserved in amber for about 53 million years, a beetle has been described as a new species by researchers in Spain and France. Named Cnopus twentyonepilotorum, it is the first puppet beetle (family Aderidae) to be formally described from the Oise amber of northern France. The findings are published in the journal ZooKeys.

articles.title: Chimpanzees blowing raspberries offer first evidence of learned vocal conventions in great ape communication
articles.source: Phys.org - latest science and technology news stories
articles.summary: Chimpanzees may learn how to use some of their calls from the adults around them, in a surprising parallel with how human children learn words, finds a study from the CNRS Institute of Cognitive Sciences, University of Warwick and Taï Chimpanzee Project.

articles.title: Don't study alone: New research shows how loneliness impacts student health—and how universities can help
articles.source: Phys.org - latest science and technology news stories
articles.summary: The negative impact of loneliness on health and well-being is well known, but for university students, social interaction can also be key to academic success. A new study by Constructor University professor Dr. Sonia Lippke and colleagues, published in the journal Frontiers in Psychology, analyzes the effects of student loneliness on health and academics and lays out concrete steps that universities can take to mitigate them.
